title: Long corolla flowers in Tropical Andes favour nectar robbing by the Black Metaltail hummingbird: A study using citizen science and field observations
orientation_basis: longer corolla = greater legitimate-access constraint; robbery increases
evidence_basis: Primary article reports nectar robbing strongly associated with longer-corolla flowers.
notes: Eligibility was frozen before direction coding.

title: When Bigger Is not Better: Corolla Length Increases Nectar Robbing in Aloe secundiflora Engl. (Asphodelaceae)
orientation_basis: longer corolla = greater legitimate-access constraint; robbery probability increases
evidence_basis: Primary article title and author report state that flowers with longer corollas have a much greater probability of nectar robbing.
notes: Eligibility was frozen before direction coding.

title: Pollinators and nectar robbers cause directional selection for large spur circle in Impatiens oxyanthera (Balsaminaceae)
orientation_basis: larger spur circle increases difficulty of legitimate nectar extraction, but robbing frequency decreases
evidence_basis: Primary article reports an obvious negative effect of spur circle diameter on robbing frequency; large spur circles increase foraging difficulty yet are less likely to be robbed.
notes: Eligibility was frozen before direction coding; oriented against the frozen access-constraint definition rather than raw trait size alone.

title: Effect of Weigela hortensis (Caprifoliaceae) floral morphology on pollinator behavior
orientation_basis: lower proportion of flowers appropriately accessible to short-proboscid Bombus = greater access constraint; robbery is more frequent
evidence_basis: Primary abstract reports Bombus hypocrita robbed more frequently at SSY, where the proportion of flowers appropriately sized for queens to reach nectaries was lower than at IZM.
notes: Eligibility was frozen before direction coding; site-level accessibility orientation used.

title: Bird extinctions shift bill–flower trait matching in Hawaiian lobelioids
orientation_basis: more negative bill-minus-flower matching = shorter bill relative to flower = greater access mismatch; robbery probability increases
evidence_basis: Primary analysis reports that as bill length approaches flower length, nectar-robbing probability decreases; therefore greater mismatch predicts more robbery.
notes: Eligible as direct evidence but remains excluded from the preregistered third-network lane by fauna rule.
